A quick walkthrough for everyday use

Project Operations Digital Twin — User & Admin Guide

This app brings your project's schedule, cost, and risk data together with real software delivery numbers, and uses Claude to point out what deserves a closer look. Claude never makes decisions — it reads the numbers and suggests what to check. You stay in control.

Sections marked Administrator only apply if you manage data imports and resets. Everything else applies to anyone using the app.

1. Signing in

You'll receive a web address, plus a username and password for one of two accounts — Program Manager or Admin CTO.

  1. Open the web address in your browser.
  2. Enter your username exactly as given (for example, Program Manager).
  3. Enter your password.
  4. Click Sign in.

Switching roles without signing out

Once you're in, look for the small person icon near the top-right of the screen. Clicking it opens a quick switcher so you can preview the app as the other role without signing out first.

2. The Command Center

This is the home screen — everything important in one view.

  • Project name, current status, and an overall health color (Green, Amber, or Red).
  • Five delivery numbers (see the next section for what they mean).
  • A trend chart showing how the overall score has moved over the last 8 weeks.
  • Colour-coded Risk and Issue panels, so the biggest problems are visible at a glance.
  • An AI Analysis panel at the bottom, where you can ask Claude to review the current numbers.

Reading the trend chart and the Risk/Issue panels

The line under the five numbers is the same overall score plotted week by week — a dot for each of the last 8 weeks. A line that's sloping downward means health has been declining over that stretch; hover over any dot to see that week's exact score.

To the right, Risks and Issues each show as a short list. Every item has one coloured badge:

  • Risks: Critical (red), High (amber), Medium (blue), Low (grey).
  • Issues: High (red), Medium (amber), Low (grey) — Issues don't have a Critical tier.

Each item shows exactly one badge, matching that Risk's Exposure or that Issue's Severity — there's no need to open the item to know how serious it is. Click Analyze Project Health with AI/Claude and Claude's recommendation will often reference these same risks and issues by ID, so it's worth glancing at this panel first.

3. Understanding your delivery numbers

Five numbers on the Command Center describe how healthy your software delivery is. They're calculated automatically — you never need to work them out by hand.

NumberWhat it tells you
Deployment FrequencyHow often you're shipping — more is generally healthier.
Avg Lead TimeHours from a change being ready to it going live. Lower is faster.
Change Fail RatePercent of releases that caused a problem. Lower is better.
Avg Recovery HoursHow long it took to fix a failed release. Lower is faster.
Rework RatePercent of releases that had to be redone. Lower is better.

These come from the DORA Data page — a log of every deployment, whether it succeeded or failed, and how long it took. You don't calculate anything here; you just review it if you want the detail behind the summary numbers.

A separate page, Telemetry Snapshot, holds a weekly history of health scores (Schedule, Cost, Risk, Change, Delivery). This is what colors the Amber or Red status you see on the Command Center — it's a trend record, not something you need to edit.

4. Running an AI analysis

  1. On the Command Center, click Analyze Project Health with AI/Claude.
  2. Wait a few seconds while Claude reviews the current numbers.
  3. Read the recommendation that appears below the button.
Claude highlights two or three things worth checking and explains why they matter together — it never decides anything for you. Every analysis is saved with the date and time it ran, so you can always see how current the advice is.

5. Project data pages

Five pages hold the structural details behind the Command Center numbers. Each works the same way: a filterable list, with edit and delete icons on the right of each row.

PageWhat it holds
ProjectThe program itself — one record, with overall status and health.
PhaseThe major stages of the program (for example, Phase 1, Phase 2).
MilestoneKey dates within each phase, with a criticality level.
RiskThings that could go wrong, ranked by exposure.
IssueThings that already have gone wrong, ranked by severity.

6. Documents

The Documents page holds the governing paperwork behind the project — charters, status reports, change requests, and meeting minutes — all in one place.

  1. Click + New Project document.
  2. Choose a document type (Charter, Status Report, and so on).
  3. Choose the file from your computer and save.

To open an existing document, click its row in the list.

7. Importing and resetting data

ADMINISTRATOR ONLY

Reached from the Command Center's Goto The Data Center Administration button. This page is where project and delivery data gets loaded in or cleared out.

Importing

  • Import Project Data — brings in Project, Phase, Milestone, Risk, and Issue records. Safe to run more than once; it updates existing records instead of duplicating them.
  • Import Telemetry — loads the weekly health-score history.
  • Import DORA Log — loads the deployment log the five delivery numbers are calculated from.

Resetting

Two buttons, both in red, both ask you to confirm before doing anything:

  • Delete All Project Data — clears Project, Phase, Milestone, Risk, and Issue.
  • Delete Telemetry & DORA Data — clears the weekly health history and the deployment log.
Uploaded documents and saved AI analyses are never touched by either button, even during a full reset.

8. Roles at a glance

RoleCan do
Program ManagerView everything, add or update risks and issues, upload documents, run AI analysis.
AdministratorEverything above, plus import and reset project and delivery data.

9. Quick troubleshooting

  • The app is slow to load the first time — normal. It sleeps after an hour of no visits and takes a minute to wake up. Just wait.
  • The AI analysis says unavailable — a temporary hiccup. Click Analyze again.
  • You don't see Data Import in the menu — expected if you're signed in as Program Manager. Only Administrator sees that page.
